A Practical Guide to Getting Fewer Wrong Answers From AI Tools

You can't eliminate AI mistakes entirely, but a handful of habits meaningfully reduce how often they happen.

REPLACE_WITH_REAL_NAME August 14, 2026

AI models generate answers based on patterns, not verified lookups, which means confident-sounding wrong answers are a structural feature of how they work, not a bug that gets fully patched out. A few concrete habits reduce how often this bites you.

Ask for sources on anything you plan to rely on, and treat the request itself as a filter: a model that can point to a specific, checkable source is working from something closer to real information, while one that produces a vague or generic citation is often signaling it's guessing.

Break large questions into smaller, checkable pieces. A single sprawling prompt asking for a full analysis gives the model room to blend accurate and invented details together in ways that are hard to spot. Asking for one specific fact at a time makes errors much easier to catch.

For anything numeric — statistics, dates, prices, specific figures — verify independently before using it anywhere that matters. This is the single highest-value habit, because numbers are where confident-sounding fabrication is both common and hardest to catch by just reading the sentence.

Finally, give the model permission to say it doesn't know. Many default toward providing an answer even when the honest response is uncertainty, and an explicit instruction to flag low-confidence answers measurably changes behavior in practice.
